# Recounting the four security rooms

## What the listings show, and what they miss

Opening the four rooms returns 35 rows between them. That is not what was said in them. A room
listing carries the messages that started a thread plus the handful of replies that were
broadcast back out - here, 31 openers and 4 broadcasts. Everything else lives underneath, and
the only way to see it is to open each thread that reports replies.

## What the thread reads add, and what they double

17 of the 31 openers report replies. Opening all 17 returns 42 rows, because a thread read hands
back its own opener alongside the replies. The replies themselves number 25, and 56 messages were
posted across the four rooms in total: 11 in general-meshworks-security, 11 in security-095, 15
in security-v1-041 and 19 in security-v3-065.

## Who is actually talking

Each opener reports how many accounts are in its thread but never says which. Those counts add up
to 25 across the 17 threads, which is the reply count again rather than a roster. Reading the
threads gives 15 distinct accounts replying. 21 accounts started a thread here, and only 3 of the
repliers never started one; between them they account for 4 of the 25 replies. The recount is
posted in general-meshworks-security with a line per room and a TOTAL line.

## Self-replies

5 of the 25 replies were posted by the same account that started the thread they
replied to. A self-reply is not a separate message type; it is an ordinary reply whose
author happens to be the person who opened that thread. It still counts as a reply and
as a message; the only question is whether the author matches the opener, thread by
thread.


The 31 openers are the messages that started threads. The 4 broadcast replies are the replies visible in the room listing — the other 21 replies live underneath threads and only appear when you open them.
